hook.line: Mariana is off to Cartagena again, and Tomás hasn't had a day off in months. English says "I wish I had...". Spanish squeezes the whole wish into one exclamation.
hook.es: ¡Quién tuviera tiempo para viajar como tú!
hook.en: I wish I had time to travel like you! (to a friend)

examples.es: ¡Quién tuviera tiempo para viajar como tú!
examples.en: I wish I had time to travel like you! (to a friend)
If only I could sleep like that!
I wish I were Simón, with no worries!
I wish I were in Medellín right now!
I wish I could cook like Vale!
I wish I had your patience! (to a friend)

rule:
*¡Quién tuviera...!* means "I wish I had...", usually about something someone else has or does. *Quién* looks like "who", but here it always means *I*, so never add *yo*.
The verb takes the *-ra* past form: *tuviera*, *pudiera*, *fuera*, *estuviera*, *supiera*. The wish is about now, even though the form looks like the past.
There is no "I wish" word at all. The exclamation marks and a sigh do the work, with a little envy and a little humour.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a wish exclamative: *quién* + imperfect subjunctive, for a wish that is hard to reach.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *tuviera* or *tuvo*, then type the whole sentence: ¡Quién ___ tiempo para viajar como tú! (I wish I had time to travel like you!)
yourTurn.answer: ¡Quién tuviera tiempo para viajar como tú!
yourTurn.why: A wish needs the *-ra* form, not the plain past.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *pudiera* or *puede*, then type the whole sentence: ¡Quién ___ dormir así! (If only I could sleep like that!)
Type it in Spanish: I wish I had your patience! (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Quién* + *tuviera* is the whole wish; there is no *yo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the question into a wish: *¿Quién puede dormir así?* becomes: If only I could sleep like that!
yourTurn.why: Change *puede* to *pudiera* and swap the question marks for exclamation marks.
